cemc-hypatia-2007-01a.title: List systematically
cemc-hypatia-2007-01a.body:
Choose the first city after $A$ (3 ways: $B$, $C$, $D$), then the second (2 ways); the third is forced. That gives $3 \times 2 = 6$ routes:

- $A \to B \to C \to D \to A$
- $A \to B \to D \to C \to A$
- $A \to C \to B \to D \to A$
- $A \to C \to D \to B \to A$
- $A \to D \to B \to C \to A$
- $A \to D \to C \to B \to A$

cemc-hypatia-2007-01b.title: Compute every route
cemc-hypatia-2007-01b.body:
Using $AB = 80$, $AC = 105$, $AD = 40$, $BC = 120$, $BD = 60$, $CD = 90$:

| Route | Length |
|---|---|
| $A\to B\to C\to D\to A$ | $80 + 120 + 90 + 40 = 330$ |
| $A\to B\to D\to C\to A$ | $80 + 60 + 90 + 105 = 335$ |
| $A\to C\to B\to D\to A$ | $105 + 120 + 60 + 40 = 325$ |
| $A\to C\to D\to B\to A$ | $105 + 90 + 60 + 80 = 335$ |
| $A\to D\to B\to C\to A$ | $40 + 60 + 120 + 105 = 325$ |
| $A\to D\to C\to B\to A$ | $40 + 90 + 120 + 80 = 330$ |

**Shortest:** $A\to C\to B\to D\to A$ (or $A\to D\to B\to C\to A$), 325 km. **Longest:** $A\to B\to D\to C\to A$ (or $A\to C\to D\to B\to A$), 335 km.

cemc-hypatia-2007-01b.title: Think about the unused roads
cemc-hypatia-2007-01b.body:
A route uses 4 of the 6 roads and skips one pair of "opposite" roads (roads with no common city): $\{AB, CD\}$, $\{AC, BD\}$ or $\{AD, BC\}$. The total of all six roads is $495$.

- Skip $AB, CD$ (sum 170): length $325$.
- Skip $AC, BD$ (sum 165): length $330$.
- Skip $AD, BC$ (sum 160): length $335$.

The shortest route skips $AB$ and $CD$: $A\to C\to B\to D\to A$ (325 km). The longest skips $AD$ and $BC$: $A\to B\to D\to C\to A$ (335 km).

cemc-hypatia-2007-01c.title: Count choices
cemc-hypatia-2007-01c.body:
In $A \to x \to y \to E \to z \to A$ there are 3 choices for $x$, then 2 for $y$, and $z$ is forced: $3 \times 2 = 6$ routes.

**Answer: 6**

cemc-hypatia-2007-01c.title: Insert E into the old routes
cemc-hypatia-2007-01c.body:
Each of the 6 routes from part (a) gives exactly one new route by inserting $E$ between the third and fourth stops, and every new route arises this way. So there are 6.

**Answer: 6**

cemc-hypatia-2007-01d.title: Use both trips
cemc-hypatia-2007-01d.body:
First trip: $AD + DC + CE + EB + BA = 40 + 90 + CE + EB + 80 = 600$, so $CE + EB = 390$.

Second trip: $AC + CD + DE + EB + BA = 105 + 90 + 225 + EB + 80 = 700$, so $EB = 200$.

Therefore $CE = 390 - 200 = 190$ km.

**Answer: 190 km**

cemc-hypatia-2007-01d.title: Subtract the trips
cemc-hypatia-2007-01d.body:
The two trips share $EB$, $BA$ and $CD$. Subtracting the first from the second:

$$(AC + DE) - (AD + CE) = 100 \implies 105 + 225 - 40 - CE = 100 \implies CE = 190.$$

**Answer: 190 km**

cemc-hypatia-2007-02a.title: Feed the small pails
cemc-hypatia-2007-02a.body:
Each legal move takes 1 from three pails and adds 3 to the fourth.

| Move | P | Q | R | S | Comment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| start | 9 | 9 | 1 | 5 | |
| 1 | 8 | 8 | 4 | 4 | 3 added to R |
| 2 | 7 | 7 | 7 | 3 | 3 added to R |
| 3 | 6 | 6 | 6 | 6 | 3 added to S |

(Other sequences also work.)

cemc-hypatia-2007-02bi.title: Target 23 each
cemc-hypatia-2007-02bi.body:
There are $31 + 27 + 27 + 7 = 92$ marbles, so the goal is 23 in each pail.

| Move | P | Q | R | S | Comment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| start | 31 | 27 | 27 | 7 | |
| 1 | 30 | 26 | 26 | 10 | 3 added to S |
| 2 | 29 | 25 | 25 | 13 | 3 added to S |
| 3 | 28 | 24 | 24 | 16 | 3 added to S |
| 4 | 27 | 23 | 23 | 19 | 3 added to S |
| 5 | 26 | 22 | 22 | 22 | 3 added to S |
| 6 | 25 | 21 | 21 | 25 | 3 added to S |
| 7 | 24 | 24 | 20 | 24 | 3 added to Q |
| 8 | 23 | 23 | 23 | 23 | 3 added to R |

(Other sequences also work.)

cemc-hypatia-2007-02bii.title: Watch pail P
cemc-hypatia-2007-02bii.body:
The total number of marbles never changes (each move moves 3 marbles), so at the end every pail has $92 / 4 = 23$ marbles.

Pail P starts with 31, so it must lose 8 marbles overall. In each move, pail P either loses exactly 1 marble or gains 3. So it takes at least 8 moves in which P loses a marble. Hence at least 8 legal moves are needed (and part (i) shows 8 is enough). ∎

cemc-hypatia-2007-02c.title: Parity
cemc-hypatia-2007-02c.body:
The total is 36, so the goal would be 9 marbles in every pail (all odd).

In a legal move every pail changes by $-1$ or $+3$, both odd numbers, so **every** pail switches parity. Starting with two even pails (10, 8) and two odd pails (11, 7), after any move we again have two even and two odd pails. So we can never reach four odd pails, i.e. never $9, 9, 9, 9$. ∎

cemc-hypatia-2007-02c.title: Differences mod 4
cemc-hypatia-2007-02c.body:
In a legal move, two pails either both change by $-1$ (difference unchanged) or one changes by $+3$ and the other by $-1$ (difference changes by 4). So the difference between any two pails never changes modulo 4.

At the end all differences would be 0. But initially $11 - 10 = 1$ is not a multiple of 4. So equal pails are impossible. ∎

cemc-hypatia-2007-03b.title: Factor the difference
cemc-hypatia-2007-03b.body:
$s^2 - 4s - 21 = t^2 - 4t - 21 \implies s^2 - t^2 - 4(s - t) = 0 \implies (s - t)(s + t - 4) = 0.$

Since $s \ne t$, we must have $s + t = 4$. (This is the only possible value, and it occurs, e.g. $s = 7$, $t = -3$.)

**Answer: $s + t = 4$**

cemc-hypatia-2007-03b.title: Axis of symmetry
cemc-hypatia-2007-03b.body:
$f(x) = (x - 2)^2 - 25$, so the parabola $y = f(x)$ is symmetric about $x = 2$. Two different inputs give the same output exactly when they are mirror images in this line, i.e. when their average is 2. So $s + t = 4$.

**Answer: $s + t = 4$**

cemc-hypatia-2007-03c.title: Factor into integers
cemc-hypatia-2007-03c.body:
As in (b): $(a^2 - 4a - 21) - (b^2 - 4b - 21) = (a - b)(a + b - 4) = 4$.

Both factors are integers whose product is 4, and their sum $2a - 4$ is even, so they have the same parity: both are $\pm 2$.

- $a - b = 2$, $a + b - 4 = 2$: $a + b = 6$, so $a = 4$, $b = 2$.
- $a - b = -2$, $a + b - 4 = -2$: $a + b = 2$, $a = 0$, $b = 2$ — not positive.

(The pairs $(1, 4), (4, 1), (-1, -4), (-4, -1)$ have odd sum, so they give non-integer $a$.)

**Answer: $a = 4$, $b = 2$**

cemc-hypatia-2007-03c.title: Use the shape of the parabola
cemc-hypatia-2007-03c.body:
$f(x) = (x - 2)^2 - 25$, so $f(a) - f(b) = (a - 2)^2 - (b - 2)^2 = 4$. Let $m = |a - 2|$, $n = |b - 2|$, non-negative integers with $m^2 - n^2 = 4$. Then $(m - n)(m + n) = 4$, where $m - n$ and $m + n$ have the same parity and $m + n \ge 0$, so $m - n = m + n = 2$, i.e. $m = 2$, $n = 0$: $b = 2$ and $a = 4$ or $a = 0$. As $a > 0$, $a = 4$.

**Answer: $a = 4$, $b = 2$**

cemc-hypatia-2007-04a.title: Join the centres
cemc-hypatia-2007-04a.body:
Centres of tangent circles are at distance $1 + 1 = 2$, so $QR = RS = PR = PS = 2$. $Q$, $R$, $S$ are all 1 unit above $BC$, so $Q$, $R$, $S$ are collinear (line parallel to $BC$).

$\triangle PRS$ is equilateral, so $\angle PSR = \angle PRS = 60^\circ$. Then $\angle QRP = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ$, and $\triangle QRP$ is isosceles with $QR = RP$, so $\angle PQR = 30^\circ$.

Thus $\angle PQS = 30^\circ$, $\angle PSQ = 60^\circ$ and $\angle QPS = 90^\circ$.

**Answer: $30^\circ$, $60^\circ$, $90^\circ$**

cemc-hypatia-2007-04a.title: R is the circumcentre
cemc-hypatia-2007-04a.body:
$RQ = RS = RP = 2$, so $P$, $Q$, $S$ lie on a circle with centre $R$ and diameter $QS$. By Thales' theorem $\angle QPS = 90^\circ$. In right triangle $QPS$, $PS = 2$ and $QS = 4$, so $\sin\angle PQS = \frac{2}{4}$, giving $\angle PQS = 30^\circ$ and $\angle PSQ = 60^\circ$.

**Answer: $30^\circ$, $60^\circ$, $90^\circ$**

cemc-hypatia-2007-04b.title: Parallel sides and angle bisectors
cemc-hypatia-2007-04b.body:
Each side of $\triangle PQS$ is parallel to a side of $\triangle ABC$ ($QS \parallel BC$, $PS \parallel AC$, $PQ \parallel AB$, since the centres are at distance 1 from the sides they touch). So $\triangle ABC$ has the same angles as $\triangle PQS$: $\angle A = 90^\circ$, $\angle B = 30^\circ$, $\angle C = 60^\circ$.

**Side $AC$.** $P$ lies on the bisector of $\angle A$, so $\angle PAC = 45^\circ$; $S$ lies on the bisector of $\angle C$, so $\angle SCA = 30^\circ$. Drop perpendiculars $PX$ and $SZ$ to $AC$ (both of length 1). $PXZS$ is a rectangle, so $XZ = PS = 2$.

- In $\triangle AXP$ ($45^\circ$): $AX = PX = 1$.
- In $\triangle CZS$ ($30^\circ$ at $C$): $CZ = \sqrt3 \cdot SZ = \sqrt3$.

So $AC = 1 + 2 + \sqrt3 = 3 + \sqrt3$.

In the $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle $ABC$ (right angle at $A$, $AC$ opposite the $30^\circ$ angle): $BC = 2AC = 6 + 2\sqrt3$ and $AB = \sqrt3\, AC = 3\sqrt3 + 3$.

**Answer: $AC = 3 + \sqrt3$, $AB = 3 + 3\sqrt3$, $BC = 6 + 2\sqrt3$**

cemc-hypatia-2007-04b.title: Compute BC directly
cemc-hypatia-2007-04b.body:
Angles as in Solution 1. Along $BC$: from the tangency point of circle $Q$ to that of circle $S$ is $QS = 4$. From $B$ to the tangency point of circle $Q$: $Q$ lies on the bisector of $\angle B = 30^\circ$, so this length is $\frac{1}{\tan 15^\circ} = 2 + \sqrt3$. From $C$ to the tangency point of circle $S$: $\frac{1}{\tan 30^\circ} = \sqrt3$.

So $BC = (2 + \sqrt3) + 4 + \sqrt3 = 6 + 2\sqrt3$, and then $AC = \frac12 BC = 3 + \sqrt3$, $AB = \frac{\sqrt3}{2} BC = 3\sqrt3 + 3$.

cemc-hypatia-2007-04c.title: Two right triangles
cemc-hypatia-2007-04c.body:
Now $PQ = PS = 2$ and $QR = RS = PR = 1 + r$. By symmetry $P$, $R$ and the tangency point $E$ of circle $R$ with $BC$ are collinear and $PE \perp BC$. Let $QS$ meet $PR$ at $Y$; then $QY \perp PR$.

$Q$ is 1 above $BC$ and $R$ is $r$ above, so $YR = 1 - r$. In $\triangle QYR$:

$$QY^2 = (1 + r)^2 - (1 - r)^2 = 4r.$$

Also $PY = PR - YR = (1 + r) - (1 - r) = 2r$. In $\triangle PYQ$: $PY^2 + QY^2 = PQ^2$, so

$$4r^2 + 4r = 4 \implies r^2 + r - 1 = 0 \implies r = \frac{-1 + \sqrt5}{2}$$

(taking the positive root).

**Answer: $r = \dfrac{\sqrt5 - 1}{2} \approx 0.618$**
